name: Muhammad I Establishes the Nasrid Emirate of Granada
summary: Muhammad I ibn al-Ahmar founds the Nasrid Emirate of Granada after the Almohad collapse. He accepts Castilian suzerainty (paying tribute and providing military assistance) in exchange for political independence, a pragmatic arrangement that ensures the emirate's survival for 254 years. The Alhambra palace complex begins construction under Muhammad I and his successors, becoming the finest surviving example of Nasrid architecture.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Nasrid strategy of accommodation and tribute payment to Castile is the most successful diplomatic approach in al-Andalus history; it preserves a Muslim state in Iberia for two and a half centuries after the Almohad collapse; the Alhambra and the cultural florescence of Nasrid Granada represents the final flower of Andalusian civilization; the emirate's fall in 1492 ends 781 years of Muslim political presence in Iberia
